"First tell me your intention."
He said,
"I once heard you say,
'To delight in Heaven and know one's destiny is why one does not worry,'
this is why I am happy."
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) looked troubled and said slowly,
"Did I say that?
Your understanding is mistaken.
Those were my words from the past;
let me now correct them with what I say today.
You only know the freedom from worry in delighting in Heaven and knowing one's destiny,
but you do not know the great worry that lies in delighting in Heaven and knowing one's destiny.
Now I will tell you the truth:
"To cultivate oneself,
accept poverty or success,
know that coming and going are not up to me,
and to be free from turmoil in one's thoughts,
this is what you call the freedom from worry in delighting in Heaven and knowing one's destiny.
Formerly, I cultivated the *Shī* (詩) and *Shū* (書),
rectified rites and music,
intending to govern the world,
and leave a legacy for future generations;
not merely to cultivate myself and govern the state of Lǔ (魯).
But the ruler and ministers of Lǔ (魯) daily lose their proper order,
benevolence and righteousness increasingly decline,
and feelings become increasingly thin.
If this Way cannot be practiced in one state or in this generation,
what will become of the world and future generations?
"I began to realize that the *Shī* (詩), *Shū* (書), rites, and music cannot save us from order or chaos,
but I do not yet know how to reform them.
This is what those who delight in Heaven and know their destiny worry about.
However,
I have found it.
To delight and to know,
is not what the ancients called delight and knowing.
Without delight, without knowing,
this is true delight and true knowing;
therefore, there is nothing that one does not delight in,
nothing that one does not know,
nothing that one does not worry about,
nothing that one does not do.
"What reason is there to abandon the *Shī* (詩), *Shū* (書), rites, and music?
Why reform them?"
Yánhuí (顏回) bowed with his face to the north and said,
"I also understand it."
He went out and told Zǐgòng (子貢).
Zǐgòng (子貢) was confused and at a loss,
returned home and pondered deeply for seven days,
without sleeping or eating,
to the point that he was reduced to skin and bones.
Yánhuí (顏回) went again to explain it to him,
and then he returned to the gate of the Kǒng (孔) family,
playing music, singing, and reciting books,
never ceasing for the rest of his life.
An official of Chén (陳) was sent to Lǔ (魯),
and privately met with Shūsūnshì (叔孫氏).
Shūsūnshì (叔孫氏) said,
"Our state has a sage."
The official said,
"Is it not Kǒngqiū (孔丘)?"
Shūsūnshì (叔孫氏) said,
"It is."
"How do you know he is a sage?"
Shūsūnshì (叔孫氏) said,
"I often hear Yánhuí (顏回)
say,
'Kǒngqiū (孔丘) can abandon his mind and use his form.'"
The official of Chén (陳) said,
"Our state also has a sage,
do you not know?"
Shūsūnshì (叔孫氏) said,
"Who do you call a sage?"
The official said,
"Among the disciples of Lǎodān (老聃)
is one Kàngcāngzǐ (亢倉子),
who obtained the Dao of Dān (聃),
and can see with his ears and hear with his eyes."
The Lord of Lǔ (魯) was greatly surprised upon hearing this,
and sent a high minister with generous gifts to invite him.
Kàngcāngzǐ (亢倉子) accepted the invitation and arrived.
The Lord of Lǔ (魯) humbly asked him about it.
Kàngcāngzǐ (亢倉子) said,
"Those who spread this rumor are wrong.
I can see and hear without using my ears and eyes,
but I cannot change the function of the ears and eyes."
The Lord of Lǔ (魯) said,
"This only increases my wonder.
What is your Way like?
I sincerely wish to hear about it."
Kàngcāngzǐ (亢倉子) said,
"My body merges with my mind,
my mind merges with my qi,
my qi merges with my spirit,
and my spirit merges with the nothingness.
If there is the slightest presence,
or the slightest sound,
even if it is far beyond the eight wildernesses,
or close within my eyebrows and eyelashes,
whatever comes to me,
I will know it.
It is not that I know it through my seven orifices and four limbs,
or that my heart and six viscera know it,
it is simply that I know it of myself."
The Lord of Lǔ (魯) was greatly pleased.
Another day, he told Zhòngní (仲尼) about it,
Zhòngní (仲尼) smiled but did not answer.
The Tài Zǎi of Shāng saw Kǒngzǐ and said,
"Qiū, are you a sage?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"A sage? How would I, Qiū, dare to be called that?
However, I am a man of broad learning and much knowledge."
The Tài Zǎi of Shāng said,
"Were the Three Kings sages?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"The Three Kings were good at employing the wise and the brave,
but as for whether they were sages, I do not know."
He said,
"Were the Five Emperors sages?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"The Five Emperors were good at employing the humane and the righteous,
but as for whether they were sages, I do not know."
He said,
"Were the Three Sovereigns sages?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"The Three Sovereigns were good at employing those who adapted to the times,
but as for whether they were sages, I do not know."
The Tài Zǎi of Shāng was greatly astonished
and said,
"Then who is a sage?"
Kǒngzǐ, with a deliberate pause, changed his expression
and said,
"There is a sage among the people of the West,
who rules without governing, yet there is no disorder;
who is self-confident without speaking;
who acts spontaneously without transformation;
so vast that the people cannot name him.
I suspect he is a sage.
I do not know if he is truly a sage
or truly not a sage."
The Tài Zǎi of Shāng was silent, calculating in his heart, and said,
"Kǒng Qiū is deceiving me!"
Zǐxià asked Kǒngzǐ,
"What kind of person is Yánhuí?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Huí's benevolence and virtue are superior to mine."
He said,
"What kind of person is Zǐgòng?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Cì's eloquence and wisdom are superior to mine."
He said,
"What kind of person is Zǐlù?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Yóu's courage and virtue are superior to mine."
He said,
"What kind of person is Zǐzhāng?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Shī's gravity and virtue are superior to mine."
Zǐxià moved from his mat and asked,
"Then why do these four gentlemen serve you, Master?"
He said,
"Sit!
I will tell you.
Huí can be benevolent but cannot be rebellious;
Cì can be eloquent but cannot be inarticulate;
Yóu can be brave but cannot be timid;
Shī can be grave but cannot be agreeable.
If I were to exchange my qualities for what the four of them have,
I would not allow it.
This is why they serve me without hesitation."
Zǐ Lièzi, having studied with Húqiū Zǐlín and befriended Bóhūn Màorén,
then lived in Nánguō.
Those who followed him numbered
more than a hundred, yet were not like him.
Even so,
Zǐ Lièzi was also subtle.
Morning after morning they argued with each other,
and no one failed to hear them.
But he lived next door to Nánguō Zǐ for twenty years
without ever visiting him or making a request;
when they met on the road,
their eyes were as if they did not see each other.
The servants and attendants at his door
suspected that Zǐ Lièzi and Nánguō Zǐ were certainly enemies.
Someone came from Chǔ
and asked Zǐ Lièzi,
"What is the nature of the enmity between you, Master, and Nánguō Zǐ?"
Zǐ Lièzi said,
"Nánguō Zǐ appears full on the outside but is empty on the inside;
his ears hear nothing,
his eyes see nothing,
his mouth says nothing,
his mind knows nothing,
his body shows no apprehension.
What would I gain by going to him?
Nevertheless,
I will try going with you."
Seeing Nánguō Zǐ,
he was indeed like a deceiving ghost, and one could not engage with him.
Looking back at Zǐ Lièzi,
his form and spirit did not match,
and one could not associate with him.
After a while, Nánguō Zǐ pointed at the disciple of Zǐ Lièzi who was walking at the end of the line and spoke with him,
cheerfully and appearing single-minded and full of vigor.
The followers of Zǐ Lièzi were astonished by this.
Returning to their residence, they all had doubtful expressions.
Zǐ Lièzi said,
"He who obtains satisfaction has no words;
he who advances in knowledge also has no words.
Using no words as words is also speaking;
using no knowledge as knowledge is also knowing.
No words and not speaking,
no knowledge and not knowing,
are both speaking and knowing.
One also speaks of everything,
one also knows everything;
one also speaks of nothing,
one also knows nothing.
It is just like that.
Why are you so needlessly alarmed?"
In Zǐ Lièzi's learning,
after three years,
his heart dared not dwell on right and wrong,
and his mouth dared not speak of profit and harm;
only then did he receive one glance from Lǎoshāng.
After five years,
his heart dwelt more on right and wrong,
and his mouth spoke more of profit and harm;
only then did Lǎoshāng crack a smile.
After seven years,
following what his heart dwelt on,
there was no longer right and wrong;
following what his mouth spoke of,
there was no longer profit and harm.
Only then did the master draw me close and sit with me on the same mat.
After nine years,
in what my heart dwelt on at random,
and what my mouth spoke of at random,
I did not know whether it was my right and wrong, profit and harm,
or whether it was the other's right and wrong, profit and harm;
the outer and inner had advanced.
And then the eyes were like the ears,
the ears were like the nose,
the nose was like the mouth;
there was no difference.
The mind congealed and the body dissolved, the bones and flesh all melted away;
one was unaware of where the body leaned,
where the feet trod, what the mind dwelt on,
or where the words were stored.
It was just like that.
Then there was no place where principle was hidden.
Initially, Zǐ Lièzi enjoyed traveling.
Húqiū Zǐ said,
"Yùkòu enjoys traveling,
what does he enjoy in traveling?"
Lièzi said,
"The pleasure of traveling
is in enjoying things without a fixed purpose.
When people travel,
they observe what they see;
when I travel,
I observe what changes.
Traveling, traveling!
No one has been able to discern my traveling."
Húqiū Zǐ said,
"Is Yùkòu's traveling really the same as others,
or is it really different from others?
For all that you see,
you also always see its changes.
You enjoy the things that have no fixed purpose,
but you do not know that I also have no fixed purpose.
You strive for outward travel,
but you do not know to strive for inner contemplation.
Outward travel
seeks fulfillment in things;
inner contemplation
takes sufficiency from oneself.
Taking sufficiency from oneself
is the height of traveling;
seeking fulfillment in things is the failure of traveling."
Thereupon, Lièzi did not go out for the rest of his life,
thinking that he did not know how to travel.
Húqiū Zǐ said,
"His traveling has reached its peak!
The ultimate traveler does not know where he is going;
the ultimate observer does not know what he is looking at.
All things are traveling,
all things are observing;
this is what I call traveling,
this is what I call observing.
Therefore, I say:
His traveling has reached its peak!
His traveling has reached its peak!"
Lóng Shū said to Wén Zhì,
"Your skill is subtle.
I have an illness;
can you cure it?"
Wén Zhì said,
Lóng Shū said,
"My village's praise, I do not consider it an honor;
the country's destruction, I do not consider it a disgrace;
gaining, I am not happy;
losing, I am not worried;
I see life as death;
I see wealth as poverty;
I see people as pigs;
I see myself as a person.
Dwelling in my home,
as if in an inn;
viewing my village,
as if it were a barbarian land.
All these many ills,
titles and rewards cannot encourage,
punishments cannot intimidate,
prosperity and decline, benefit and harm cannot change,
sorrow and joy cannot move.
Indeed, I cannot serve a ruler,
befriend relatives,
manage wife and children,
control servants.
What is this illness?
What remedy can cure it?"
Wén Zhì then ordered Lóng Shū to stand with his back to the light,
and Wén Zhì himself looked at him from behind, facing the light.
After a moment, he said,
"Ah!
I see your heart:
the space within is empty.
Almost a sage!
Your heart has six orifices that are flowing,
but one orifice is blocked.
Now, using sagely wisdom as an illness,
perhaps it is from this!
It cannot be cured by my shallow skills."
That which has no origin and is eternally alive is the Dao.
Born from birth,
therefore, though it ends, it does not perish;
this is constant.
Born into death,
is unfortunate.
That which has an origin and is eternally dead,
is also the Dao.
Dying from death,
therefore, though it has not ended, it perishes on its own,
is also constant.
Born from death,
is fortunate.
Therefore, to be born without use is called the Dao,
and to use the Dao to obtain the end is called constancy;
to die with use is also called the Dao,
and to use the Dao to obtain death is also called constancy.
Jì Liáng's death,
Yáng Zhū looked at his gate and sang.
Suí Wú's death,
Yáng Zhū stroked his corpse and wept.
The life of a servant,
the death of a servant,
the crowd will sing,
and the crowd will weep.
Eyes about to be dim, first see an autumn hair;
ears about to be deaf, first hear a gnat fly;
mouth about to be tasteless, first distinguish Zī and Miǎn;
nose about to be blocked, first sense charred decay;
body about to be stiff, first run swiftly and freely,
heart about to be lost, first recognize right and wrong:
therefore, things that do not arrive do not return.
Zhèng's Pǔ Zé had many worthies,
Dōng Lǐ had many talents.
In the service of Pǔ Zé, there was one Bó Fēngzǐ,
who, passing through Dōng Lǐ,
encountered Dèng Xī.
Dèng Xī looked at his disciples and laughed, saying,
"If we were to dance, what would that one coming here be like?"
His disciples said,
"We would like to know."
Dèng Xī said to Bó Fēngzǐ,
"Do you know the meaning of 'nourishing nourishment'?
Those who receive nourishment and cannot nourish themselves,
are like dogs and pigs;
those who nourish things and things are used by me,
are the strength of men.
To make your disciples
eat and be full,
dress and rest,
is the accomplishment of the government.
For the young and old to gather together
and become things for pens, mats, kitchens,
how are they different from dogs and pigs?"
Bó Fēngzǐ did not respond.
Bó Fēngzǐ's follower stepped forward and said,
"Has the noble not heard of the many machines of Qí and Lǔ?
There are those skilled in managing earth and wood,
there are those skilled in managing metal and leather,
there are those skilled in managing sound and music,
there are those skilled in managing writing and numbers,
there are those skilled in managing armies,
there are those skilled in managing ancestral temples,
a gathering of talents is prepared.
But without a prime minister,
there is no one to command their use.
Those who position them are without knowledge,
those who command them are without ability,
and knowledge and ability
are made to serve them.
Those who govern are, in fact, those who we command;
what are you arrogant about?"
Dèng Xī had nothing to say in response,
he signaled his disciples and retreated.
Gōngyí Bó was known among the feudal lords for his strength,
Tángxī Gōng spoke of him to King Xuān of Zhōu,
and the King prepared elaborate gifts to hire him.
Gōngyí Bó arrived;
observing his appearance,
he was a weakling.
King Xuān was confused and doubtful, saying,
"What is your strength like?"
Gōngyí Bó said,
"My strength can break the thigh of a spring locust,
and can bear the wing of an autumn cicada."
The King changed his expression and said,
"My strength can tear rhinoceros and buffalo hide,
drag the tail of nine oxen,
yet still regret its weakness.
You break the thigh of a spring locust,
and bear the wing of an autumn cicada,
and are known throughout the world for your strength,
why?"
Gōngyí Bó sighed deeply and retreated from his mat, saying,
"Excellent
is the King's question!
I dare to answer truthfully.
My teacher was Shāngqiū Zǐ,
whose strength was unmatched in the world,
yet his six relatives did not know;
because he never used his strength.
I serve him with my life.
He then told me,
'People want to see what they have not seen,
to observe what people do not spy;
to obtain what they have not obtained,
to cultivate what people do not do.
Therefore, those who learn to see first see a cartload of firewood,
those who learn to listen first hear a bell struck.
If there is ease within,
there is no difficulty without.
If there is no difficulty without,
then fame does not leave its single path.'
Now my name is known among the feudal lords,
this is because I have violated my teacher's teachings,
and shown off my ability.
In that case, my fame is not because of bearing my strength,
but because of being able to use my strength;
is it not better than bearing strength?"
Gōngzǐ Móu of Zhōngshān was
a worthy prince of the state of Wèi.
He liked to associate with worthies,
and did not care about affairs of state;
and he admired Gōngsūn Lóng of Zhào.
The followers of Yuèzhèng Ziyú laughed at him.
Gōngzǐ Móu said,
"Why do you laugh at my admiration for Gōngsūn Lóng?"
Ziyú said,
"Gōngsūn Lóng's character is such that
his actions have no teacher,
his learning has no friends,
he is glib but not accurate,
rambling and without a home,
he likes strangeness and speaks wildly.
He wants to deceive people's minds,
to silence people's mouths,
and practices this with Hán Tán and others."
Gōngzǐ Móu changed his expression and said,
"Why do you describe Gōngsūn Lóng's faults?
Please tell me the truth."
Ziyú said,
"I laugh at Lóng's deception of Kǒng Chuān,
saying
'A skilled archer
can make the following arrow hit the front nock,
each shot reaching the next,
arrows connected to each other;
the front arrow reaches the target
without falling,
the nock of the following arrow is still on the string,
looking as if they are one.'"
Kǒng Chuān was astonished by this.
Lóng said:
"This is not the most marvelous thing.
Féng Méng's disciple, named Hóng Chāo,
became angry with his wife and frightened her.
He drew his Wūhào bow,
with Qí Wèi's arrow,
and shot at her eye.
The arrow came and aimed at the pupil,
but her eyelid did not even twitch.
The arrow tunneled into the ground without raising any dust."
Are these the words of a wise man?"
Gōngzǐ Móu said:
"The words of a wise man
are certainly not understood by a fool.
The later arrow hits the preceding notch,
equaling the latter with the former.
The arrow aims at the pupil but the eyelid does not twitch;
this is the full potential of the arrow.
What do you doubt?"
Yuèzhèng Ziyú said:
"You and Lóng's followers,
how can you not embellish their flaws?
I will tell you something even more egregious.
Lóng deceived the King of Wèi, saying:
'There is intention without mind,
there is pointing without reaching,
there is something without being exhausted,
there is a shadow without moving,
a hair can lift a thousand *jūn*
A white horse is not a horse.
A lone calf never had a mother.'
His denial of categories and reversal of ethics
cannot be fully expressed."
Gōngzǐ Móu said:
"You do not understand profound words and consider them egregious;
the fault lies with you.
Without intention, minds are the same;
without pointing, all reach.
Those who exhaust things always have something.
That the shadow does not move
is explained by change.
A hair can lift a thousand *jūn*;
when the force is at its peak, they are equal.
A white horse is not a horse;
form and name are separate.
A lone calf never had a mother; if it has a mother, it is not a lone calf."
Yuèzhèng Ziyú said:
"You consider all of Gōngsūn Lóng's pronouncements as principles.
Suppose they emanated from some other hole,
you would also accept them."
Gōngzǐ Móu was silent for a long time,
then took his leave, saying:
"Please allow me to wait for another day
to discuss with you again."
Yáo ruled the world for fifty years,
not knowing whether the world was well-governed
or not well-governed.
He did not know whether the multitudes wished to support him
or did not wish to support him.
He asked those around him,
but those around him did not know.
He asked the outer court,
but the outer court did not know.
He asked those in the countryside,
but those in the countryside did not know.
Yáo then traveled in plain clothes on the main road,
and heard children singing a rhyme:
"He established us, the common people,
none are not from your ultimate source.
Knowing nothing, understanding nothing,
we follow the rules of the Emperor."
Yáo happily asked:
"Who taught you to say these words?"
The children said:
"We heard it from the officials."
He asked the officials.
The officials said:
"It is an ancient poem."
Yáo returned to the palace,
summoned Shùn,
and then ceded the world to him.
Shùn accepted it without declining.
Guān Yǐnxī said:
"When being is not fixated on itself,
forms of things will be clearly manifested.
Its movement is like water,
its stillness is like a mirror,
its response is like an echo.
Therefore, its *dào* is like things themselves.
Things themselves deviate from the *dào*;
the *dào* does not deviate from things.
One who is good at following the *dào*
also does not use ears,
also does not use eyes,
also does not use force,
also does not use the mind.
To desire to be like the *dào* and use sight, hearing, form, and intelligence to seek it
is not appropriate.
Look for it in the front,
and suddenly it is in the back;
use it, and it fills everything; the six voids
discard it, and no one knows where it is.
It is not something that those with intention can obtain from afar,
nor is it something that those without intention can obtain from nearby.
Only those who obtain it in silence and whose nature completes it obtain it.
Knowing without emotion,
being able without acting,
is true knowing and true ability.
If there is no arising of knowledge,
how can there be emotion?
If there is no arising of ability,
how can there be action?
Gathering clumps,
accumulating dust,
although there is no action, it is not without principle."
Yīn Tāng asked Xià Gé:
"Was there something in the ancient beginning?"
Xià Gé said:
"In the ancient beginning there was nothing;
how could there be something now?
Would later people say that there was nothing now? Is that acceptable?"
Yīn Tāng said:
"Then things have no before and after?"
Xià Gé said:
"The end and beginning of things
initially had no ultimate limit.
The beginning may become the end,
the end may become the beginning;
how can one know its order?
However, beyond things themselves,
before events themselves,
this is what I do not know."
Yīn Tāng said:
"Then do up, down, and the eight directions have an ultimate end?"
Gé said:
"I do not know."
Tāng firmly asked.
Gé said:
"If there is nothing, then there is no limit;
if there is something, then there is an end.
How would I know this?
However, beyond the unlimited
there is again no unlimited;
within the unending
there is again no unending.
The unlimited is again not unlimited,
the unending is again not unending.
By this, I know that there is no limit and no end,
but I do not know if there is a limit and an end."
Tāng again asked:
"What is beyond the Four Seas?"
Gé said:
"It is like Qízhōu."
Tāng said:
"How do you substantiate this?"
Gé said:
"I traveled east to Yíng,
and the people were still the same.
I asked about the east of Yíng,
and again it was like Yíng.
I traveled west to Bīn,
and the people were still the same.
I asked about the west of Bīn,
and again it was like Bīn.
By this, I know that beyond the Four Seas,
the Four Desolations, and the Four Limits, it is no different from here.
Therefore, large and small contain each other,
without ultimate limit.
That which contains all things is also like containing Heaven and Earth.
Because it contains all things, it is without end;
because it contains Heaven and Earth, it is without limit.
How would I also know that beyond the surface of Heaven and Earth there is not a great Heaven and Earth?
This is also what I do not know.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth are also things.
Things have deficiencies;
therefore, in the past, Nǚwā clan refined five-colored stones to repair its gaps,
and cut off the feet of the *Ao* turtle to establish the Four Extremes.
Later, Gònggōng clan and Zhuānxū struggled to be emperor,
and in anger, he struck Mount Bùzhōu,
breaking the pillars of Heaven,
severing the cords of Earth;
therefore, Heaven tilted to the northwest,
and the sun, moon, and stars went there;
the Earth was not full in the southeast,
therefore, hundreds of rivers and waters return there."
Tāng again asked:
"Do things have large and small?
Do they have long and short?

and Qiū Bǐng Zhāng's son, Lái Dān, plotted to avenge his father's death.
Dān's anger was intense,
and his intentions were obvious;
he counted his grains as he ate,
and he ran with the wind.

he could not raise an army to avenge himself.
Ashamed to borrow strength from others,
he swore to slaughter Hēi Luǎn with his own sword.
Hēi Luǎn was fierce and surpassed the crowd,
his strength equal to a hundred men.
His sinews, bones, skin, and flesh
were unlike those of ordinary men.
He could extend his neck to receive a blade,
or expose his chest to receive an arrow.
The sharpest edges would bend and break,
but his body would bear no marks or wounds.
Relying on his strength,
he saw Lái Dān as no more than a fledgling.
Lái Dān's friend, Shēn Tā, said,
"Your hatred for Hēi Luǎn is extreme,
but Hēi Luǎn's contempt for you is even greater.

Lái Dān, with tears streaming down his face, said,
"I wish you would devise a plan for me."
Shēn Tā said,

met Kǒng Zhōu,
performed the ceremony of a servant and driver,

for you to choose;

it vanishes without a trace,
passing through an object without the object noticing.

at the intersection of dawn and dusk,
at the boundary of sunset and twilight,
facing north and observing it,
faintly, it seems something exists,
but no one can discern its shape.
When it touches something,
there is a faint, rustling sound,
passing through an object without harming it.
The third is Xiāo Liàn,
in broad daylight, one sees its shadow but not its light,
at night, one sees its light but not its form.
When it touches something,
it swiftly passes through,
closing up immediately after,
one feels a swiftness, but no blood is drawn.
These three treasures
have been passed down for thirteen generations,
yet never used in action.

never having been opened."
Lái Dān said:

sighed and returned home.

met me at the door,

also causing my body to ache and my limbs to feel stiff.

equally pacifies it,
readies it and welcomes it."
